To merge the last two commits in Git, you can use the following steps:

1. Use the `git log` command to view the commit history and identify the commit hashes of the last two commits that you want to merge.

2. Use the `git rebase -i HEAD~2` command to open an interactive rebase window for the last two commits.

3. In the interactive rebase window, you can choose to squash the last two commits into a single commit by changing the word "pick" to "squash" (or "s" for short) next to the commit that you want to squash into the previous commit.

4. Save and close the rebase window. Git will then combine the last two commits into a single commit.

5. If there are any merge conflicts during the rebase process, resolve them as instructed by Git.

6. Finally, use the `git log` command to verify that the last two commits have been successfully merged into a single commit.

7. Optionally, you can use `git push --force` to push the changes to the remote repository, but be cautious as this will alter the commit history for others working on the same repository.
